text:
maria: Heads up — last 3 nights we've had repeated pages for `gpu-node-oom-group` in us-west-2. Mostly between 00:10–00:25 and they auto-resolve. Paging noise is killing oncall. Thoughts on moving these to ticketing with a longer dedupe window?

sam: Do we have a correlation with the nightly batch jobs or autoscaler churn? If it's predictable pattern tied to cron, ticketing makes sense, otherwise we risk missing real issues.

julian: We previously tried grouping by `node_label` and that over-grouped across prod/test. Alternative: per-region rolling window + severity. Suggestion: page if >3 distinct nodes in 10m, else create ticket. Example alert rule sketch:```yaml
alert: GPUNodeOOMGroup
expr: increase(gpu_node_oom_total[10m]) > 3
for: 0m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "us-west-2 GPU node OOM spike"
```
This keeps short spikes ticketed, sustained problems page.

ops-bot: alert gpu-node-oom-group fired (us-west-2) count=1 severity=ticket — auto-silenced by schedule at 00:12:09

ira: Also consider a "hand-off safety margin": if pages happen inside the nightly maintenance window, suppress paging and create ticket. Add a cooldown per oncall team so repeated 1-off flaps don't wake people.

devon: From a cost perspective, paging for transient OOMs is expensive (human-hours). I'd start with a 20m mute window + ticket, then monitor ticket backlog and escalate rules if backlog grows.

sam: Agreed, but let's keep a progressive escalation: ticket -> watch (dashboard alert) -> page if (a) persists for 15m OR (b) error rate >5% across requests. That reduces noise while still catching incidents.

julian: I'll open a PR to change the alert and add a Grafana panel to show "pages avoided" vs "ticketed incidents". @maria can you review the PR when I post it? I'll include the runbook edit.

maria: :thumbsup: will review later today.

oncall: Note — changing this rule will require a playbook update and reassigning runbook ownership. I've pinged the rotation owners in case we need a temporary contact during rollout.

julian: Thanks — I'll add a short canary period (48h) and a rollback plan. If we see missed pages during the canary we'll revert and tighten thresholds.

maria: Sounds good. If the PR lands, let's also add a job that reports "page->ticket ratio" daily so we can tune thresholds empirically.

sam: I'll draft a follow-up ticket for the metrics and dashboard queries.

julian: PR link will land in #eng-releases when ready.

(ends)
